question:
Select the correct option of the given sentence.

Smt. Savithri is wisest than all others in the group.
option_1: Smt. Savithri is the wiser than all others in the group.
option_2: Smt. Savithri is wise than all others in the group.
option_3: Smt. Savithri is wiser than all others in the group.
option_4: Smt. Savithri is the wise than all others in the group.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Smt. Savithri is wiser than all others in the group.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "than" is a signal of the comparative degree. The given sentence wrongly uses the superlative "wisest" with "than". The comparative of "wise" is "wiser".

◦ Correct: Smt. Savithri is wiser than all others in the group.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 wrongly adds the article "the" before the comparative ("the wiser than"). "The" is used with the superlative (the wisest), not with a comparative followed by "than".

• Options 2 and 4 use the positive degree "wise", which cannot be used with "than".

NOTE

• Degrees of "wise": wise (positive) – wiser (comparative, used with "than") – wisest (superlative, used with "the"). Never mix a superlative form with "than".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The teacher asked the students to stay _________ during the exam.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. quiet.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Quiet" (adjective) means silent, making little or no noise; calm. Students are asked to stay quiet (silent) during the exam. (शांत / चुप)

◦ Correct: The teacher asked the students to stay quiet during the exam.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "quite" is an adverb meaning "fairly/completely" and does not fit here.

• Option 3 "quote" means to repeat someone's words; Option 4 "quit" means to leave/give up. Both are unrelated.

NOTE

• Do not confuse quiet (silent) with quite (to a certain extent). Spelling tip: quiet = silent (both end in a "t").

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

He received the best employee award because he was the more hardworking.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. most hardworking.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "the best employee award" and the definite article "the" call for the superlative degree. So "the more hardworking" (comparative) should be "the most hardworking" (superlative).

◦ Correct: He received the best employee award because he was the most hardworking.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "hardworking" (positive) and Option 4 "the hardworking" do not convey that he was the topmost among all employees.

• "the more" (comparative) is wrong because a comparison of one against a whole group needs the superlative.

NOTE

• Long adjectives form the superlative with "the most" (the most hardworking) and the comparative with "more ... than" (more hardworking than).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Due to _________ 'eve teasing', parents conclude that it is not worth the danger of sending their daughters to school.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. widespread.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Widespread" means existing or happening over a large area or among many people; prevalent. Because eve teasing is widespread (very common everywhere), parents feel it is too dangerous to send their daughters to school. (व्यापक)

◦ Correct: Due to widespread 'eve teasing', parents conclude that it is not worth the danger ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "rectified" (corrected) contradicts the negative sense of the sentence.

• Option 2 "narrow" and Option 3 "localised" (limited to a small area) suggest the problem is small, which does not justify parents' fear.

NOTE

• Synonyms of widespread: prevalent, extensive, rampant, pervasive. Antonyms: rare, limited, scarce, localised.

question:
Select the word that has the same meaning (SYNONYM) as the underlined word in the given sentence.

The teacher made judicious use of technology to explain a sensitive topic.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. prudent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Judicious" means showing good judgement; wise, sensible and careful in making decisions. Its closest synonym is "prudent" (careful and sensible). (विवेकपूर्ण / समझदार)

◦ Example: She made a judicious/prudent decision to save money for the future.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "difficult" and Option 2 "prominent" (famous/important) are unrelated in meaning.

• Option 4 "judgmental" (overly critical of others) is a false friend — it looks similar to "judicious" but has a negative sense.

NOTE

• Synonyms of judicious: prudent, wise, sensible, discerning, shrewd. Antonyms: injudicious, foolish, rash, imprudent.

question:
Read the following sentence and select its future tense form from the options given below:

Ramya finished her dissertation early.
option_1: Ramya had finished her dissertation early.
option_2: Ramya will finish her dissertation early.
option_3: Ramya has finished her dissertation early.
option_4: Ramya is finishing her dissertation early.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Ramya will finish her dissertation early.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence is in the simple past tense ("finished"). Its simple future form uses "will + base verb (V1)" → "will finish".

◦ Correct: Ramya will finish her dissertation early.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "had finished" is past perfect.

• Option 3 "has finished" is present perfect.

• Option 4 "is finishing" is present continuous.

NOTE

• Simple future = subject + will/shall + base form of the verb (will go, will finish, shall write). It expresses an action that will happen later.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

He possesses one of the slimmer handsets in the world.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. slimmest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "one of the + superlative + plural noun" is used to say something is among the best/top examples. So it must be "one of the slimmest handsets in the world".

◦ Correct: He possesses one of the slimmest handsets in the world.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "most slim" and Option 3 "most slimmest" are wrong — short adjectives like "slim" form the superlative with "-est" (slimmest), not with "most", and "most slimmest" is a double superlative.

• Option 4 "slim" (positive) does not fit the "one of the ..." structure.

NOTE

• "One of the tallest boys", "one of the best players", "one of the slimmest phones" — always superlative + plural noun.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Exhilerate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Exhilerate" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "exhilarate", meaning to make someone feel very happy, excited and full of energy. (उत्साहित करना / रोमांचित करना)

◦ Spelling key: EX + HIL + A + RATE.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• The other options are correctly spelt: "incorrigible" (impossible to correct or reform), "mischievous" (naughty, causing trouble) and "amendment" (a change or correction).

NOTE

• Note the common error in "mischievous" — it has no "i" before "ous" (not "mischievious"). Related word: exhilaration (noun).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The branches of the tree is very long.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. are.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject of the sentence is "The branches" (plural), so it needs a plural verb. The correct verb is "are", not the singular "is".

◦ Correct: The branches of the tree are very long.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The phrase "of the tree" is only a modifier; the real subject is "branches" (plural). This is a case of the "attraction error" where the nearby noun "tree" (singular) tempts us to use "is".

• Options 1 "had", 2 "was" and 4 "has" are all singular/wrong here.

NOTE

• Subject-verb agreement rule: ignore the words between the subject and verb ("of the tree"). "The branches ... are"; "The quality of the mangoes is good".

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Celibrate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Celibrate" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "celebrate", meaning to mark a happy or important occasion with festivities. (उत्सव मनाना)

◦ Spelling key: CE + LE + BRATE.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The other options are correctly spelt: "abandoned" (deserted/given up), "dangerous" (risky) and "excellent" (extremely good).

NOTE

• Do not confuse "celebrate" (to rejoice) with "celibate" (a person who abstains from marriage/sexual relations) — different words entirely.

question:
select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank to complete the idiom and make the sentence meaningful.

During the interview, the candidate was challenged to provide chapter and ___________ on his proposed plan.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. verse.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "chapter and verse" means exact and full details / precise information about something. The candidate was asked to give chapter and verse — i.e., complete, detailed information — on his plan. (पूरा ब्यौरा / सटीक जानकारी)

◦ Correct: ... the candidate was challenged to provide chapter and verse on his proposed plan.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "page", "lines" and "cover" do not form a standard idiom in this structure.

NOTE

• The idiom originates from precise references to the Bible (chapter and verse number). Similar idioms of detail: "ins and outs", "the nitty-gritty".

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word..
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. tendancy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Tendancy" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "tendency", meaning an inclination or a natural disposition to behave in a particular way. (प्रवृत्ति / झुकाव)

◦ Spelling key: TEN + DEN + CY (ends in "-ency", not "-ancy").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• The other options are correctly spelt: "resistance" (the act of opposing), "separate" (to divide/apart) and "weather" (the atmospheric condition).

NOTE

• Common spelling trap: "separate" has an "a" in the middle (sep-A-rate), not "seperate". "Weather" (climate) vs "whether" (if).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word provided in the brackets to fill in the blank.

The painting exhibited a __________________ blend of colours. (harmonious)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. discordant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Harmonious" means pleasingly combined; in agreement / blending well together. Its antonym is "discordant", meaning clashing, not in harmony, disagreeing. (सामंजस्यपूर्ण का विलोम — बेमेल / असंगत)

◦ Correct: The painting exhibited a discordant blend of colours.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "quavering" (trembling, of the voice) and Option 3 "thrilling" (exciting) are unrelated.

• Option 2 "polyphonic" (having many sounds/voices) is not an antonym of harmonious.

NOTE

• Synonyms of harmonious: congruous, agreeable, melodious. Antonyms: discordant, jarring, clashing, incompatible.

question:
Select the appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

At the drop of a hat
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Willingness to do something instantly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "at the drop of a hat" means immediately, without any hesitation or delay; readily. (तुरंत / बिना किसी देरी के)

◦ Example: He is always ready to help his friends at the drop of a hat.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• The idiom comes from the old practice of signalling the start of a race or a fight by dropping a hat.

• The other options do not match the accepted meaning of the idiom.

NOTE

• Similar idioms of promptness: "in a flash", "in the blink of an eye", "without batting an eyelid", "on the spot".

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

The place where soldiers live
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Barracks.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Barracks" is the one-word substitute for the place/building where soldiers live. (सैनिकों के रहने का स्थान — बैरक)

◦ Example: The soldiers returned to their barracks after the parade.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Unit", Option 2 "Regiment" and Option 3 "Brigade" refer to groups/formations of soldiers, not to the place where they live.

• A regiment and a brigade are military units made up of several battalions/companies.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes: arsenal (a place for storing weapons), garrison (troops stationed in a fortress/town), cantonment (a permanent military station).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

David decided to __________ his old boat to get a new one.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. sell.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sell" is a verb meaning to give/hand over something in exchange for money. After "decided to", we need the base form of a verb, so "sell" is correct. (बेचना)

◦ Correct: David decided to sell his old boat to get a new one.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "sale" is a noun (the act of selling), not a verb — "decided to sale" is wrong.

• Option 3 "cell" (a small room / a unit of life or a battery) and Option 4 "ceil" are unrelated homophones.

NOTE

• Verb vs noun: "sell" (verb) / "sale" (noun) — "They sell cars; there is a sale today." After "to", use the base verb form.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The Chinese government has accepted slower economic development as the 'new normal', recognising the need for China to adopt a new growth model that depends less on fixed investment and exports and more on private consumption, services, and innovation to _____________ economic growth.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. drive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Drive" here means to push forward / propel / stimulate. China wants private consumption, services and innovation to drive (boost/promote) economic growth. (आगे बढ़ाना / गति देना)

◦ Correct: ... more on private consumption, services, and innovation to drive economic growth.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "exhale" (to breathe out) and Option 3 "success" (a noun, not a verb) do not fit grammatically or in meaning.

• Option 4 "bridle" means to restrain/control, which is the opposite of promoting growth.

NOTE

• "Drive growth", "drive change", "drive innovation" are common collocations meaning to power or stimulate something. Synonyms: propel, boost, spur, fuel.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in bold in the given sentence.

It is universally acknowledged that trees are indispensable to us.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Essential.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Indispensable" means absolutely necessary; something that cannot be done without. Its closest synonym is "essential". (अनिवार्य / अपरिहार्य)

◦ Example: Water is indispensable/essential for life.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Unusual" (uncommon), Option 3 "Rational" (logical) and Option 4 "Fierce" (aggressive/violent) are unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of indispensable: essential, vital, crucial, necessary, imperative. Antonyms: dispensable, unnecessary, optional, superfluous.

question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

Yesterday was the worse day of my life.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. worst.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The definite article "the" and the comparison with the whole of "my life" require the superlative degree. The superlative of "bad" is "worst" (bad – worse – worst).

◦ Correct: Yesterday was the worst day of my life.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "worse" is the comparative (used with "than"), so "the worse day" is wrong.

• Option 1 "most bad" is not standard English; Option 2 "ill" and Option 4 "bad" (positive) do not fit "the ... day of my life".

NOTE

• Irregular degrees: bad – worse – worst and good – better – best. Use the superlative with "the" (the worst).

question: Which of the following sentences contains an adverbial error?
option_1: He sang beautifully at the talent show.
option_2: The teacher spoke clear and concise.
option_4: They danced gracefully across the stage.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The teacher spoke clear and concise.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• To describe how the action "spoke" was done, we need adverbs, not adjectives. "clear and concise" are adjectives; they should be "clearly and concisely".

◦ Correct: The teacher spoke clearly and concisely.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• The other sentences use adverbs correctly: "sang beautifully", "writes slowly and steadily", "danced gracefully".

NOTE

• Adverbs modify verbs and usually answer "how?" (often ending in "-ly"): beautifully, clearly, quickly. Adjectives (clear, concise, quick) modify nouns, not verbs.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

It is the mad (1)_______ for speed that is responsible for many motor accidents. Only last year, I (2)_______ what might have been a (3)_______ accident on Kashmir Road. I was motoring down (4)________ Srinagar; and as I was nearing Kohala, I came upon the (5)_______ of two cars on the road.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. craze.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Craze" means a great and often temporary enthusiasm or obsession for something. "The mad craze for speed" (a wild obsession with driving fast) fits the theme of motor accidents. (सनक / दीवानगी)

◦ Correct: It is the mad craze for speed that is responsible for many motor accidents.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "boredom" (dullness), Option 3 "luck" (fortune) and Option 4 "block" (obstruction) do not fit the sense of an obsessive desire for speed.

NOTE

• "The mad craze for speed" describes reckless fast driving. Synonyms of craze: obsession, mania, fad, fascination.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

It is the mad (1)_______ for speed that is responsible for many motor accidents. Only last year, I (2)_______ what might have been a (3)_______ accident on Kashmir Road. I was motoring down (4)________ Srinagar; and as I was nearing Kohala, I came upon the (5)_______ of two cars on the road.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. witnessed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Witnessed" means saw something happen (especially an event or incident). The narrator "witnessed" what might have been a fatal accident. (देखा / गवाह बना)

◦ Correct: Only last year, I witnessed what might have been a fatal accident on Kashmir Road.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "anticipated" (expected beforehand) and Option 3 "checked" (examined/stopped) do not suit "what might have been ... accident".

• Option 4 "argued" (debated) is unrelated to seeing an event.

NOTE

• To "witness" an event = to see it happen. Related noun: witness (a person who saw an incident). Synonyms: observe, see, watch.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

It is the mad (1)_______ for speed that is responsible for many motor accidents. Only last year, I (2)_______ what might have been a (3)_______ accident on Kashmir Road. I was motoring down (4)________ Srinagar; and as I was nearing Kohala, I came upon the (5)_______ of two cars on the road.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. fatal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fatal" means causing or capable of causing death. A serious motor accident that "might have been" deadly is a fatal accident. (घातक / जानलेवा)

◦ Correct: ... what might have been a fatal accident on Kashmir Road.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "wonderful" (delightful) and Option 4 "harmless" (causing no harm) contradict the serious, negative tone.

• Option 3 "happening" does not fit as an adjective before "accident".

NOTE

• Synonyms of fatal: deadly, lethal, mortal, disastrous. Note: "fatal" (deadly) vs "fateful" (having important consequences).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

It is the mad (1)_______ for speed that is responsible for many motor accidents. Only last year, I (2)_______ what might have been a (3)_______ accident on Kashmir Road. I was motoring down (4)________ Srinagar; and as I was nearing Kohala, I came upon the (5)_______ of two cars on the road.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. from.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The preposition "from" indicates the starting point of a journey/movement. "I was motoring down from Srinagar" shows the narrator was driving away from Srinagar (towards Kohala). (से — यात्रा का आरंभ बिंदु)

◦ Correct: I was motoring down from Srinagar ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "on", Option 3 "since" (used for time, not place of departure) and Option 4 "besides" (in addition to) do not fit the movement "down ... Srinagar".

NOTE

• "Motoring/driving down from (a place)" means travelling away from that place. "From" marks the source/origin of movement; "to" marks the destination.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

It is the mad (1)_______ for speed that is responsible for many motor accidents. Only last year, I (2)_______ what might have been a (3)_______ accident on Kashmir Road. I was motoring down (4)________ Srinagar; and as I was nearing Kohala, I came upon the (5)_______ of two cars on the road.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. collision.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Collision" means a crash in which two moving objects (here, two cars) strike each other violently. The narrator "came upon the collision of two cars on the road". (टक्कर / भिड़ंत)

◦ Correct: ... I came upon the collision of two cars on the road.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "clatter" (a rattling noise), Option 3 "cluster" (a group of similar things) and Option 4 "pile" (a heap) do not describe two cars crashing.

NOTE

• Synonyms of collision: crash, smash, impact, accident. Related word: "collide" (verb) — the two cars collided.

question: With reference to agriculture in India, the term 'penda' is the name given to ________________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is slash and burn agriculture.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In India, "penda" is a local name for slash and burn agriculture (shifting cultivation) — a practice in which forest land is cleared by cutting and burning vegetation, cultivated for a few years, and then abandoned. (झूम / स्थानांतरी कृषि)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Slash and burn (shifting) cultivation is known by different local names across India: Jhum (North-East), Podu (Andhra/Odisha), Penda/Bewar/Dahiya (Madhya Pradesh/Chhattisgarh), Kumari (Western Ghats).

• It is common among tribal communities in hilly and forested regions.

NOTE

• Such agriculture leads to deforestation and soil erosion, and yields are low. Globally it is called by names like "milpa" (Mexico) and "ladang" (Indonesia/Malaysia).

question: Which of the following states has the lowest child sex ratio according to Census of India, 2001?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Haryana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of India, 2001, Haryana recorded the lowest child sex ratio (0–6 years) among the given states, at about 819 girls per 1000 boys. (हरियाणा — सबसे कम बाल लिंगानुपात)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Child sex ratio is the number of girls per 1000 boys in the 0–6 years age group.

• A low child sex ratio reflects social problems like female foeticide and gender bias. Punjab and Haryana have historically shown low ratios.

NOTE

• As per Census 2011, the overall sex ratio of India was 943 females per 1000 males, and the child sex ratio was 919 — the lowest since independence. Kerala has the highest overall sex ratio.

question: Which of the following is the first event in a triathlon?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Swimming.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A triathlon is an endurance event consisting of three continuous stages performed in the order: Swimming → Cycling → Running. Thus, the first event is Swimming. (ट्रायथलॉन — तैराकी पहले)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The standard Olympic (ITU) triathlon consists of a 1.5 km swim, 40 km cycle and 10 km run.

• Triathlon became an Olympic sport at the Sydney 2000 Games.

NOTE

• "Putting the shot" (shot put) is an athletics field event and is not part of a triathlon. A "biathlon" combines skiing and shooting; a "pentathlon" and "decathlon" are multi-event athletics competitions.

question: 'Ace Against Odds' is the autobiography of a sports personality playing the game of ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tennis.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ace Against Odds" is the autobiography of the ace Indian tennis player Sania Mirza. (टेनिस — सानिया मिर्ज़ा की आत्मकथा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sania Mirza was a World No. 1 in women's doubles and won six Grand Slam titles (doubles and mixed doubles). She received the Padma Bhushan and the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna.

• The word "ace" in tennis means a serve that the opponent cannot touch.

NOTE

• Other sports autobiographies: Playing It My Way (Sachin Tendulkar), The Test of My Life (Yuvraj Singh), Unbreakable (Mary Kom), Straight from the Heart (Kapil Dev).

question: As per Census 2011, which of the following states recorded negative growth in child sex ratio?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per Census 2011, among the given options Maharashtra recorded a negative growth (decline) in child sex ratio compared to 2001. Its child sex ratio fell to around 894, showing a downward trend. (महाराष्ट्र — बाल लिंगानुपात में गिरावट)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The child sex ratio (0–6 years) of India declined from 927 (2001) to 919 (2011) — the lowest since independence.

• A falling child sex ratio points to persistent gender discrimination and female foeticide.

NOTE

• States like Punjab and Haryana, though still low, actually improved their child sex ratio between 2001 and 2011, whereas several richer states saw declines.

question: The excavated ruins of the Nalanda University indicate that bright red _____ was/were used in its construction.
solution_text:
The correct answer is bricks.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The excavated ruins of the ancient Nalanda University (Bihar) show that bright red bricks were used extensively in its construction. (नालंदा — लाल ईंटें)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Nalanda was a great Buddhist Mahavihara (residential university) founded in the 5th century CE during the Gupta period (by Kumaragupta I). It flourished under patronage from the Guptas and later King Harsha and the Palas.

• It was destroyed by the invader Bakhtiyar Khalji around 1193 CE.

• The Chinese travellers Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang) and I-Tsing studied and described Nalanda.

NOTE

• The ruins of Nalanda Mahavihara were declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site (2016). A modern Nalanda University was re-established in Rajgir, Bihar in 2014.

question: Which of the following factors is primarily responsible for soil formation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Weathering.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Weathering" — the breaking down of rocks into fine particles by physical, chemical and biological processes — is the primary factor responsible for soil formation. (अपक्षय — मृदा निर्माण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Soil formation (pedogenesis) depends on five factors: parent rock/material, climate, relief (topography), organisms (flora and fauna), and time.

• Physical (mechanical) weathering breaks rocks apart; chemical weathering alters their composition; biological weathering involves plants, animals and microbes.

NOTE

• Irrigation, mining and degradation do not create soil; degradation and mining, in fact, harm the soil. The uppermost fertile layer of soil is the topsoil (humus-rich).

question: In January 2023, three Indian-origin researchers were among nine scientists named recipients of the Blavatnik Awards for Young Scientists in the UK. Which of the following is NOT one of these three scientists?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gagandeep Kang.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In January 2023, the three Indian-origin scientists among the Blavatnik Awards for Young Scientists (UK) honourees were Mehul Malik, Rahul R Nair and Tanmay Bharat. Gagandeep Kang was NOT one of them. (गगनदीप कांग — इसमें शामिल नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Dr. Gagandeep Kang is a renowned Indian virologist/microbiologist, famous for her work on rotavirus vaccines; she was the first Indian woman to be elected a Fellow of the Royal Society (2019).

• The Blavatnik Awards honour outstanding young scientists and are funded by the Blavatnik Family Foundation.

NOTE

• Rahul R Nair works on graphene/2D materials; Tanmay Bharat is a structural biologist; Mehul Malik works in quantum physics/photonics.

question: Shovana Narayan, a Padma Shri recipient, is an exponent of ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Shovana Narayan, a Padma Shri recipient, is a renowned exponent of the Kathak classical dance form. (कथक — शोवना नारायण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kathak is the classical dance of North India (Uttar Pradesh), derived from the word "katha" (story). It is known for its fast footwork (tatkar), spins (chakkars) and expressive storytelling.

• Its main gharanas are Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (UP), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: According to sympatric speciation, the rising of a new species occurs when:
option_1: one species is separated into different groups due to geologic events like mountain formation
option_2: organisms from the same species start to show different behavioural characteristics
option_3: two groups of the same species cannot interbreed among themselves despite living in the same geographic location
option_4: the two groups of organisms from the same species would phenotypically look different
solution_text:
The correct answer is two groups of the same species cannot interbreed among themselves despite living in the same geographic location.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In sympatric speciation, a new species arises when two groups of the same species become reproductively isolated (cannot interbreed) even though they live in the same geographic area — without any physical/geographical barrier. (समवृत्ति जातीयकरण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• This is different from allopatric speciation, where a species is split by a geographical barrier (like a mountain or river — Option 1).

• In sympatric speciation, isolation arises through mechanisms like polyploidy, changes in mating preference, or ecological niche differences.

NOTE

• Speciation is the formation of new and distinct species. Key types: Allopatric (geographic separation), Sympatric (same area) and Parapatric (adjacent, partly overlapping populations).

question: Despite being eligible for the job of a Legal Officer, Mr. X was not called for an interview for the aforementioned post. Which of his rights was Mr. X unable to exercise?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Equality of opportunity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When an eligible candidate is denied a chance to be interviewed for a public post, the right violated is "Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment", guaranteed by Article 16 of the Constitution. (अवसर की समानता — अनुच्छेद 16)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Article 16 ensures equality of opportunity for all citizens in matters relating to employment or appointment to any office under the State.

• It is part of the Right to Equality (Articles 14–18).

NOTE

• Article 14 — equality before law and equal protection of laws.

• Article 15 — prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth.

• Article 21A — Right to Education.

question: Which of the following cultural festivals of Himachal Pradesh is organised on the auspicious occasion of Basant Panchami at Hadimba Temple?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Doongri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Doongri fair/festival" is celebrated on the occasion of Basant Panchami at the Hadimba (Hidimba Devi) Temple in Manali, Himachal Pradesh. (डूंगरी मेला — हडिम्बा मंदिर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Hadimba Devi Temple in Manali is dedicated to Hidimba, wife of Bhima (of the Mahabharata), and is a famous wooden pagoda-style temple.

• Himachal Pradesh is known for colourful fairs and festivals like the Kullu Dussehra, Minjar Fair (Chamba) and Lavi Fair (Rampur).

NOTE

• Option 3 "Mopin" is a festival of Arunachal Pradesh (Galo tribe) and Option 4 "Ziro" refers to the Ziro Music Festival of Arunachal Pradesh — not of Himachal Pradesh.

question: In May 2023, the Union Housing and Urban Affairs Ministry has extended the deadline of its Smart Cities Mission to ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is June 2024.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In May 2023, the Union Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs extended the deadline of the Smart Cities Mission to June 2024 (to complete ongoing projects). (स्मार्ट सिटीज मिशन — जून 2024)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Smart Cities Mission was launched on 25 June 2015 to develop 100 smart cities with core infrastructure, a clean and sustainable environment, and "smart" solutions.

• It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme implemented through Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs).

NOTE

• Other urban missions launched in 2015: AMRUT (Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation) and PMAY-Urban (Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Housing for All).

question: Where was the Hindustani classical singer Kumar Gandharva born?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The legendary Hindustani classical singer Kumar Gandharva (real name Shivaputra Siddheshwar Komkali) was born in 1924 at Sulebhavi in Belgaum district, Karnataka. (कुमार गंधर्व — कर्नाटक में जन्म)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kumar Gandharva was known for his unconventional, independent style and his renditions of nirgun bhajans and folk-influenced compositions.

• He was honoured with the Padma Bhushan (1977) and Padma Vibhushan (1990).

NOTE

• The title "Kumar Gandharva" (a divine celestial musician) was given to him in his childhood in recognition of his extraordinary musical talent.

question: Who among the following scholars gave reference to the history of Kashmir?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kalhana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kalhana, a 12th-century Kashmiri historian, wrote the "Rajatarangini" ("River of Kings"), a chronicle giving a detailed history of Kashmir and its kings. (कल्हण — राजतरंगिणी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Rajatarangini (written around 1148–1150 CE in Sanskrit) is regarded as one of the earliest works of true historical writing in India.

• It is a major source for the medieval history of Kashmir.

NOTE

• Other famous court poets/scholars: Banabhatta (wrote Harshacharita and Kadambari in Harsha's court), Kalidas (Abhijnanashakuntalam, Meghaduta, Raghuvamsha).

question: The author of 'Arthashastra' was a contemporary of which of the following rulers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chandragupta Maurya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Arthashastra" was written by Kautilya (Chanakya / Vishnugupta), who was the chief minister and adviser of Chandragupta Maurya, the founder of the Maurya Empire. Thus, the author was a contemporary of Chandragupta Maurya. (चाणक्य — चंद्रगुप्त मौर्य के समकालीन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Arthashastra is an ancient Sanskrit treatise on statecraft, economics, administration and military strategy.

• Chandragupta Maurya established the Maurya Empire around 321 BCE with Chanakya's help, overthrowing the Nanda dynasty.

NOTE

• The Arthashastra was rediscovered and published by R. Shamasastry in 1909. Chanakya is also called the "Indian Machiavelli".

question: In which of the following years was the Child Marriage Restraint Act passed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1929.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Child Marriage Restraint Act" (also known as the Sarda Act) was passed in 1929. It fixed the minimum age of marriage at 14 for girls and 18 for boys. (बाल विवाह निषेध अधिनियम — 1929)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Act was named after its sponsor Harbilas Sarda.

• It came into effect on 1 April 1930 and applied to all of British India.

NOTE

• Currently, the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 governs this area, fixing the minimum marriage age at 18 for women and 21 for men. Other social reform laws: Sati Regulation Act 1829, Widow Remarriage Act 1856.

question: Sunil Chhetri made history by becoming the first Indian to score a hat-trick in the Hero ISL, which came in the ________ edition.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2015.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sunil Chhetri became the first Indian to score a hat-trick in the Hero Indian Super League (ISL) in the 2015 edition (playing for Mumbai City FC). (सुनील छेत्री — 2015 संस्करण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Sunil Chhetri is the captain of the Indian national football team and one of the highest international goal-scorers of his generation.

• The Indian Super League (ISL) is India's top-tier professional football league, launched in 2014.

NOTE

• Sunil Chhetri was honoured with the Padma Shri, Arjuna Award and the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award (2021) — becoming the first footballer to receive the Khel Ratna.

question: The classical dance form 'Kathakali' traces its origin to which of the following states of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Kathakali" is a classical dance-drama form that traces its origin to the state of Kerala. It is famous for its elaborate costumes, colourful facial make-up (chutti), masks and expressive gestures. (कथकली — केरल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kathakali typically enacts stories from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Puranas.

• It combines dance, drama, music and elaborate mime, traditionally performed by male dancers.

NOTE

• Other classical dances of Kerala: Mohiniyattam (the graceful "dance of the enchantress"). The eight recognised classical dances of India include Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya.

question: What is the primary function of the excretory system in animals?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Removal of waste products.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The primary function of the excretory system is the removal of metabolic waste products (like urea, excess salts and water) from the body to maintain a stable internal environment. (उत्सर्जन तंत्र — अपशिष्ट निष्कासन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• In humans, the main excretory organs are the kidneys, which filter blood and produce urine. The excretory system also includes the ureters, urinary bladder and urethra.

• Other organs that help in excretion: skin (sweat), lungs (CO₂) and liver.

NOTE

• The functional unit of the kidney is the nephron. The process of removing nitrogenous waste is called excretion; maintaining water/salt balance is osmoregulation.

question: Article 157 of the Constitution of India mentions the qualifications required for appointment of the _________________ of a State.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Governor.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 157 of the Constitution of India lays down the qualifications for appointment as the Governor of a State. (अनुच्छेद 157 — राज्यपाल की योग्यताएँ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• As per Article 157, a person must (a) be a citizen of India and (b) have completed 35 years of age to be appointed Governor.

• The Governor is the constitutional head of a State and is appointed by the President (Article 155) and holds office during the President's pleasure (Article 156).

NOTE

• Article 153 — there shall be a Governor for each State.

• Article 154 — executive power of the State is vested in the Governor.

• Article 163 — Council of Ministers to aid and advise the Governor.

question: Which of the following is NOT an example of public goods?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Driveway at our home.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "driveway at our home" is a private good — it is owned and used by one household, and others can be excluded from it. Hence it is NOT a public good. (घर का ड्राइववे — निजी वस्तु)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Public goods are non-excludable (no one can be prevented from using them) and non-rivalrous (one person's use does not reduce availability for others). Examples: national defence, law enforcement/street lighting and clean air.

• Public goods are usually provided by the government because private markets tend to under-supply them (the "free-rider" problem).

NOTE

• Types of goods in economics: Private goods (excludable & rivalrous), Public goods (non-excludable & non-rivalrous), Common goods and Club goods.

question: At which of the following places was the Indian Civil Service Examination held for the first time in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Allahabad.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indian Civil Service (ICS) Examination was held for the first time in India at Allahabad (in 1922). Earlier, the examination was conducted only in London. (इलाहाबाद — भारत में पहली बार ICS परीक्षा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Until 1922, the ICS exam was held only in London, making it very difficult for Indians to appear. Satyendranath Tagore became the first Indian to clear the ICS in 1863.

• The Federal Public Service Commission, set up under the Government of India Act 1935, later became the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) after independence.

NOTE

• The UPSC was constituted on 1 October 1926 (as the Public Service Commission) and is a constitutional body under Articles 315–323 of the Constitution.

question: The Pitti Bird Sanctuary is located in which Union Territory/State of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lakshadweep.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Pitti (Bird) Sanctuary", also called Pitti Island Bird Sanctuary, is located in the Union Territory of Lakshadweep. It is an important nesting ground for sea birds like terns. (पिट्टी पक्षी अभयारण्य — लक्षद्वीप)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Lakshadweep is India's smallest Union Territory, a group of coral islands in the Arabian Sea; its capital is Kavaratti.

• Pitti Island is an uninhabited coral islet and a protected breeding site for migratory sea birds.

NOTE

• Lakshadweep is known for its coral reefs, lagoons and rich marine biodiversity. India's coral island groups are Lakshadweep (Arabian Sea) and parts of the Andaman & Nicobar Islands (Bay of Bengal).

question: Which inorganic compound is known to undergo solid state reaction to form urea?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ammonium cyanate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ammonium cyanate (NH₄OCN / NH₄CNO)" is the inorganic compound that, on heating, rearranges (a solid-state reaction) to form urea (NH₂–CO–NH₂) — an organic compound. (अमोनियम सायनेट → यूरिया)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• This famous experiment was performed by Friedrich Wöhler in 1828 and is known as the Wöhler Synthesis.

• It disproved the "Vital Force Theory" (which claimed organic compounds could be made only by living organisms), by preparing an organic compound (urea) from an inorganic one.

NOTE

• Reaction: NH₄OCN → (heat) → NH₂CONH₂ (urea). This is regarded as the beginning of modern organic chemistry. Urea is widely used as a nitrogenous fertiliser.
